title: Fairness and Bias in Multimodal AI: A Survey

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewed via Embedding Association Tests (WEAT, EATs), the Bipol metric, Spearman rank-based correlation, and the HONEST score which measures the probability of a language model outputting hurtful text given a specific template.

Reviewed via the Implicit Association Test (IAT), Word Embedding Association Test (WEAT), assessing word embeddings for collective in-group word associations, and performance disparity evaluations on demographically balanced datasets like FairFace.

Reviewed via visual interpretation tools like Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (GRAD-CAM) to generate saliency maps that detect whether models focus on objectified body regions (e.g., chest) versus non-objectified regions (e.g., face), using datasets like SOBEM.
Reviewed via the Implicit Association Test (IAT) and Word Embedding Association Test (WEAT) to measure implicit preferences and term associations between young and old people.

Reviewed using comprehensive multimodal benchmarks (e.g., MultiBench), question-answering templates crafted to reflect specific societal prejudices (e.g., BBQ), and harm categorization sets (e.g., BEAVERTAILS).
